absence_proof_requires: capture completeness confirmed for the specific rule
all decisive events share one capture-local monotonic clock epoch
the required actor attribution is proven
the rule-specific observation window is complete

authority_policy.formal_erratum_override: Only a separately published VDA erratum that identifies the affected version and exact clause may override that clause.
authority_policy.released_schema_role: Machine-readable syntax authority. It does not override conflicting prose in the published PDF.
authority_policy.tagged_source_role: Convenience mirror and source-navigation aid. The tagged README states that the published PDF prevails on disagreement.
authority_policy.github_discussions_role: Issues, pull requests, answers, labels, and milestones are non-normative unless incorporated into a published version or qualifying formal erratum.

rules.title: Repeated order applicability cannot be established

required_observations: two order messages with the same parseable orderId
a parseable orderUpdateId on both messages
unknown_when: either orderUpdateId is missing or cannot be represented by the selected parser contract

does_not_claim: which participant caused the incomplete observation

rules.title: Changed semantic content under a repeated order/update identity

required_observations: two order messages with equal orderId and orderUpdateId
the versioned comparator returns SEMANTICALLY_CHANGED

decision_contract.fleet_control_attribution_requires: trusted actor mapping proves that fleet control published the repeated order

does_not_claim: that section 6.1.4.5 assigns a sender-side obligation to fleet control
that the mobile robot accepted or rejected either message

rules.title: Repeated order content is not semantically decidable

required_observations: two order messages with equal orderId and orderUpdateId
the versioned comparator returns SEMANTICALLY_UNKNOWN

does_not_claim: that the order contents are equal

rules.title: Mobile-robot response to changed content under the current order/update identity

required_observations: the mobile robot's current orderId and current orderUpdateId are established
a later order has those same identifiers
the versioned comparator returns SEMANTICALLY_CHANGED
trusted actor mapping proves the state publisher is the mobile robot

additional_requirements_not_yet_evaluate: the new order is not taken into the internal buffer
the previous order remains in the internal buffer
execution of the previous order continues
the warning remains until a new order is accepted

does_not_claim: that JSON byte equality defines same content
that observing one state proves internal-buffer behavior or continued physical execution
rules.implementation_guard: The engine requires a trusted mobile-robot state between the first and repeated order messages that identifies the same participant, orderId, and orderUpdateId. Without it, applicability is UNKNOWN and the verdict is UNEVALUATED.

rules.title: Order graph node-edge sequence continuity

required_observations: a complete order payload containing nodes and edges
trusted actor mapping proves that fleet control published the order

evaluated_assertions: sequenceId is continuous across node-edge-node traversal
the number of edges equals the number of nodes minus one
each edge sequenceId lies between its adjacent node sequenceIds
does_not_claim: that all base/horizon update and release constraints are evaluated
that the mobile robot accepted the order

rules.title: newBaseRequest without an observable responsive order update

informative_vda_context.note: Defines the mobile robot's base-request behavior.
Defines the newBaseRequest state field as a trigger for fleet control to send a new base.

required_observations: newBaseRequest is true in a mobile-robot state
the observation window can see relevant fleet-control order publications
order identity matching is possible

decision_contract.absence_can_be_decisive_only_when: all common absence-proof requirements and the configured response window are satisfied

does_not_claim: that braking or a physical stop occurred
a normative violation unless a future source/profile supplies the missing obligation

rules.title: ONLINE publication after the mobile robot comes online

required_observations: a prior OFFLINE or CONNECTION_BROKEN state, when relevant to the incident
independent evidence that the mobile-robot MQTT client subsequently came online in a new or resumed connection epoch
a rule-complete connection-topic capture for that epoch
trusted actor mapping proves the connection publisher is the mobile robot

does_not_claim: that an OFFLINE publication alone proves a later reconnect
that wall-clock elapsed time proves a deadline
rules.implementation_guard: The engine requires the same known participant and a changed, non-empty participant connection epoch after OFFLINE. Without independent reconnect evidence, the verdict remains INCONCLUSIVE.

rules.title: cancelOrder action lifecycle reaches a terminal state

required_observations: a cancelOrder instant action whose publisher is attributed to fleet control
the cancel actionId is parseable
the capture contains the mobile-robot actionStates through completion or failure
trusted actor mapping proves the state publisher is the mobile robot

expected_protocol_response.active_matching_order: cancelOrder reports RUNNING while required movement/actions remain, then FINISHED after they stop or finish

does_not_claim: that a terminal protocol state proves the physical robot stopped safely
that every action's cancelAllowed behavior is evaluated in the current subset
rules.implementation_limitation: The current subset checks for a later terminal state associated with the cancel actionId; full movement, order, node, edge, and per-action transition validation remains future work.
